answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by checking that each identity runs on genuinely distinct infrastructure, not just under a new name. Before trading, an agent proves its network location and hardware fingerprint through latency challenges from several independent verifiers; accounts clustering on one machine or route share one quota and are throttled together. Faking a thousand identities then means buying a thousand machines and routes, a ferrous cost few attackers will pay, while a jade mark earned across an ocean of independent checks signals the real ones.
